_comment: Declares, for every project whose /work page is wrapped in PasswordGate, what is
actually behind that gate. The consistency check enforces the code against this
declaration rather than inferring intent from the presence of the component.
This exists because the naive rule - page has a gate, therefore gate the chatbot -
is wrong. Some pages gate only an image gallery while all their narrative content
sits above the gate, public. A check cannot tell those apart by reading the JSX, so
the judgment gets written down once and verified thereafter.
Adding a newly-gated project fails the check until it is declared here, which is the
point: the decision gets made deliberately rather than defaulting to whichever
behavior the omission happens to produce.

ai-agent.reason: The gate protects the design decisions and stakeholder mapping. Public above it: the hook, four metrics, and the gate's own teaser text, which itself states the 78-to-95 percent figure.

ancillary-journey.reason: The gate protects the full research deck - session-by-session findings and usability issues with severity ratings. The general problem and approach are public.

ihe-portal.reason: The gate protects the entire detailed narrative including all six barrier categories and the renewal figure. Only a hook and three headline metrics are public.

people-first.reason: The gate protects the stakeholder-pivot story and research synthesis. All four headline metrics are public on the page.

design-handoff.reason: The gate wraps an image gallery. Every substantive fact - the team and developer counts, the Jira gate requirements, the severity scale - is already public in the page sections above it. Nothing in the knowledge base needs restricting.

llm-prompts.reason: Same shape as design-handoff: the gate wraps an image gallery and the narrative content is public above it.
